map.name: Build & Decode
map.testedVersion: Static/source audit + tester runtime feedback; current Drive artifact v1.1.0

bugs.title: Creative-built entities can survive plot reset into later rounds
bugs.problem: The active builder is intentionally placed in Creative and can construct vanilla block-created entities such as an Iron Golem inside the plot. Plot cleanup resets blocks with fill air and removes only a narrow tagged transient allowlist (items, XP orbs and selected projectiles). Non-transient player-created entities are not part of the cleanup footprint, so they can survive round reset and arena reuse.
bugs.expected: All gameplay-significant mutations that an ordinary builder can create inside the authored plot must either be prevented or included in the arena reset baseline before the next round/session becomes active.
bugs.observed: The builder can create an Iron Golem from ordinary Creative blocks. The reset removes the construction blocks but the entity is not matched by the cleanup allowlist and therefore can remain in the arena after the round.
reproduction: Enter an active round as the builder in Creative mode.
Inside the active build plot, place four iron blocks in a T shape and add a carved pumpkin to create an Iron Golem.
Allow the round to end and the normal plot reset to run.
Start the next round or reuse the same arena.
Confirm the plot blocks are reset but the created Iron Golem can remain because it is outside the cleanup entity allowlist.
bugs.aiAnalysis: ArenaService gives the builder Creative mode and protects specific dangerous items, including spawn eggs, but ordinary iron blocks and carved pumpkin remain valid build materials. The cleanup path resets plot blocks and only removes arena/match-tagged minecraft:item, minecraft:xp_orb, minecraft:arrow, minecraft:snowball and minecraft:egg entities. Player-created persistent entities such as minecraft:iron_golem are not included, so the mutation footprint is larger than the reset footprint.

relevantCode.reason: Builder role enters Creative mode; clean/reset logic clears plot blocks but only removes a narrow transient entity allowlist.
Round setup/role flow authorizes the active builder to construct inside the plot before cleanup.

bugs.suggestedFix: Make reset ownership match the complete builder capability surface. Prefer removing/cleaning all non-authored entities inside the current arena/plot generation, or explicitly prevent vanilla entity-construction patterns if those entities are not part of gameplay. Keep cleanup arena- and generation-scoped.
mustPreserve: Normal Creative building with allowed blocks.
Arena isolation between the four replicas.
Authored map entities and presentation entities outside the reset ownership scope.

bugs.title: Temporary coordinate picker is reachable by normal Creative builders
bugs.problem: A normal builder can hold a stick and trigger production debug tooling, cancelling block interaction and exposing coordinate JSON unrelated to gameplay.
bugs.expected: Temporary coordinate tooling is removed from production or restricted to developer/admin users.
bugs.observed: Any builder holding a normal stick can trigger the imported coordinate picker without an admin requirement.
reproduction: Enter a Build & Decode building phase as the active Creative builder.
Obtain and hold a normal Minecraft stick.
Interact with a block.
Confirm normal interaction is cancelled and coordinate/debug output is shown.
bugs.aiAnalysis: Production main.js imports the temporary debug-stick module. That module subscribes directly to block interaction, explicitly requires no admin tag, and the arena interaction guard lets stick interactions pass through.

relevantCode.reason: Imports the temporary debug-stick module into the production entry point.
Implements the non-admin stick coordinate picker and debug output.

bugs.suggestedFix: Remove the debug-stick import from production or gate the existing tool behind the current developer/admin permission owner.
mustPreserve: Normal gameplay stick behavior must remain available when the developer tool is disabled.

bugs.title: A fully departed team can remain eligible to win the match
bugs.problem: After a match has started, Exit to Lobby and offline-expiry remove players from the active members roster but preserve their player/team records for resumability/history. Final team standings are then built from all historical state.players records rather than the active/eligible members roster. In a match with three or more teams, one team can fully leave after scoring, the remaining teams can continue, and the departed team can still be declared the winner and persisted into leaderboard results.
bugs.expected: A team with no active eligible members after explicit exit or expiry must not remain eligible for the final winner set. Historical contribution may be retained for audit/statistics only if it is explicitly separated from final winner eligibility.
bugs.observed: depart()/expire() remove players from state.members but leave state.players/playerTeams after the match has started. teamStandings() enumerates Object.keys(state.players), and resultFields() derives winnerTeamIds/winnerIds from that historical roster.
reproduction: Start a team match with at least three active teams.
Let Team A obtain the highest score.
Have every Team A player use Exit to Lobby, or allow them to expire after disconnect, while at least two other teams remain active.
Allow the remaining teams to complete the match without surpassing Team A's score.
Observe that Team A remains in final standings and can be declared/persisted as the winner even though it has no active members.
bugs.aiAnalysis: Active-session continuation correctly uses state.members and requires at least two active teams, but final-result eligibility switches ownership to the historical state.players ledger. TeamRules.teamStandings(state) explicitly calls activeTeamIds(state, Object.keys(state.players)) and also derives each team's member list from Object.keys(state.players). GuessTheBuildManager.resultFields() then builds winner IDs from those standings, and MatchResults persists them. The contradiction is deterministic from source.

relevantCode.reason: depart() removes the player from state.members but, after the match has started, intentionally retains state.players/playerTeams.
expire() removes expired players from state.members but retains their historical player/team records while allowing play to continue if two active teams remain.
teamStandings() derives final teams and members from Object.keys(state.players), not the active eligible state.members roster.
resultFields() derives winnerTeamIds and winnerIds directly from teamStandings().
Completed results persist the derived winner IDs and lifetime stats.

bugs.suggestedFix: Separate historical participant/contribution records from final-result eligibility. Derive winner-eligible teams from the authoritative active/eligible roster at terminal commit, while preserving historical score data only according to the intended forfeit policy.
mustPreserve: Reconnect/resumability history for temporarily offline players.
Previously earned contribution data according to the intended forfeit policy.
Exact-once result persistence and leaderboard accounting.

bugs.title: Drawn teams are persisted as Wins
bugs.problem: The match UI explicitly classifies equal top scores as a Draw, but resultFields() places every tied leading team into winnerTeamIds/winnerIds. MatchResults then increments each tied player's persistent wins counter. That wins field is displayed to players and is also used as a global leaderboard tie-breaker.
bugs.expected: A Draw should preserve the draw result and completed-match/score accounting without incrementing the persistent Win counter for every tied team, unless the product intentionally defines a draw as a win everywhere.
bugs.observed: The result presentation says Draw while all tied leading teams are written as winners and each tied player gains +1 Win. Persistent Wins can then affect leaderboard ordering.
reproduction: Start a normal team match with at least two teams.
Finish the match with two or more teams tied for the highest score.
Confirm the match summary/result UI displays Draw.
Open the leaderboard/personal stats after the result is committed.
Confirm players on every tied top team received an additional Win.
bugs.aiAnalysis: GuessTheBuildManager.matchSummary() uses the explicit Draw presentation whenever multiple teams share the top score. The same manager's resultFields() nevertheless classifies all top-scoring teams as winnerTeamIds and all of their members as winnerIds. MatchResults._apply() increments wins for any player in winnerIds. LeaderboardService then sorts equal totalScore entries by wins, so the semantic mismatch can alter persistent ranking.

relevantCode.reason: Displays Draw for multiple leaders but also returns every tied leader as a winner.
Increments persistent wins for every player in winnerIds on completed matches.
Exposes wins and uses wins as the second global ranking sort key after totalScore.
Player-facing result and personal-stat surfaces distinguish Draw from Wins.

bugs.suggestedFix: Represent terminal outcome semantics explicitly: when multiple top teams tie, persist a draw with no winner IDs (or a separate tiedTeamIds field) and do not increment wins. Keep total score and games played accounting unchanged.

bugs.title: Creative equipment can persist across role changes, exit and replay
bugs.problem: The builder is placed in Creative mode, but the canonical player reset helper clears only the inventory container. It never clears the separate equippable slots such as armor/offhand. A builder can therefore equip Creative-obtained gear and carry it into a later Adventure guesser role, lobby state, reconnect recovery or subsequent session.
bugs.expected: Role/session cleanup must restore the complete managed player state, including equipment/offhand acquired during Creative builder access, before the player becomes a guesser, returns to lobby or starts another session.
bugs.observed: clearInventory() removes inventory container slots only. No gameplay cleanup path clears minecraft:equippable slots, while builder Creative access allows equipment acquisition and use.
reproduction: Enter an active round as the builder in Creative mode.
Equip a Creative-obtained armor/chest/offhand item, for example an Elytra or shield.
Finish the round so the player becomes a guesser, or use Exit to Lobby and then join another session.
Observe the normal inventory cleanup/role transition.
Confirm the equipped item is not owned by clearInventory() and can remain equipped across the transition.
bugs.aiAnalysis: ArenaService.clearInventory() only accesses the minecraft:inventory component container and clears its slots. Repository-wide gameplay paths do not clear minecraft:equippable equipment slots. Because the authored builder role grants ordinary Creative catalog access, equipment state is a reachable mutable resource and must be part of reset/recovery ownership.

relevantCode.reason: Defines clearInventory() using only minecraft:inventory and invokes it for role setup, departure and recovery transitions.
Switches builder/guesser roles and Creative/Adventure state across rounds while relying on the shared inventory cleanup.

bugs.suggestedFix: Extend the canonical player-state reset owner to clear managed equipment/offhand slots through the equippable component in addition to the inventory container. Keep one reset helper rather than adding role-specific cleanup paths.
mustPreserve: Normal role rotation between builder and guesser.
Intentional map-owned equipment if any is later introduced.

bugs.title: Guess action temporarily disables Exit to Lobby
bugs.problem: The Guess item and Exit to Lobby item share the same minecraft:cooldown category and both use a two-second cooldown. Bedrock applies cooldowns by category, so using Guess also places Exit on cooldown even though leaving the match is a separate control.
bugs.expected: Guess anti-spam cooldown should not disable the player's independent Exit to Lobby control.
bugs.observed: Both builddecode:guess and builddecode:exit_game use cooldown category wind_charge for two seconds, so activating one temporarily cools down the other.
reproduction: Enter an active guessing phase with both Guess and Exit to Lobby items available.
Use the Guess item.
Immediately switch to Exit to Lobby and attempt to use it within two seconds.
Confirm Exit remains on the shared cooldown instead of being independently usable.
bugs.aiAnalysis: The item definitions independently assign the same minecraft:cooldown category, wind_charge, to Guess, Exit to Lobby, and the lobby selector item. Bedrock cooldown semantics apply to every item sharing a category. This is a deterministic cross-item configuration collision rather than a form/UI timing issue.

relevantCode.reason: Defines minecraft:cooldown category wind_charge with duration 2.
Defines the same minecraft:cooldown category wind_charge with duration 2.
Also reuses wind_charge, confirming the category is not scoped to Guess.

bugs.suggestedFix: Give Guess and Exit distinct map-owned cooldown categories (for example builddecode_guess and builddecode_exit), or remove the Exit cooldown if it has no independent need. Do not share a generic vanilla category across unrelated controls.

bugs.title: Time bonus thresholds do not match the authored scoring table
bugs.problem: Correct guesses receive the wrong time bonus for several elapsed-time ranges. The authored scoring table defines 8/10/15/25/30/50-second thresholds, while the scoring function checks 5/10/15/20/30 and never checks 8, 25, or 50.
bugs.expected: Time bonuses follow the selected artifact's Points.timebonus table: +10 through 8s, +5 through 10s, +4 through 15s, +3 through 25s, +2 through 30s, +1 through 50s, then 0.
bugs.observed: The scoring function gives +5 instead of +10 through 8s, +2 instead of +3 from 16-25s, and 0 instead of +1 from 31-50s. These points feed player/team scores and can change standings and persisted leaderboard results.
reproduction: Start a normal Build & Decode match and reach an active guessing round.
Make a correct guess within 8 seconds and compare the awarded time bonus with the Points.timebonus table.
Repeat with a correct guess at 16-25 seconds and at 31-50 seconds.
Confirm the effective bonuses are +5, +2, and 0 instead of +10, +3, and +1.
bugs.aiAnalysis: GuessTheBuildData.js defines the authored timebonus thresholds as 8, 10, 15, 25, 30, and 50 seconds. GuessRules.getTimeBonus() instead iterates [5, 10, 15, 20, 30]. Missing keys are skipped, so the next lower configured reward or default is returned. The defect is deterministic from source and does not require runtime proof.

relevantCode.reason: Lines 17-24 define the authored time-bonus thresholds and reward values.
Lines 103-110 use a different threshold list when calculating the bonus.
The returned time bonus is added directly to correct-guess points and persisted into player/team scoring.

bugs.suggestedFix: Use the canonical thresholds from Points.timebonus (or derive/sort the numeric keys) instead of maintaining a second hard-coded threshold list.

bugs.title: Blocked water placement can leave client-only waterlogged residue
bugs.problem: Blocked bucket use can leave water visually lodged in barrier or other waterloggable blocks for the acting player while server state remains unchanged.
bugs.expected: A rejected water placement leaves no water or waterlogged visual on any client.
bugs.observed: Tester runtime shows the acting player can retain water/waterlogged visuals after placement is rejected; other clients do not share the state.
reproduction: Enter a Build & Decode building phase as the active builder.
Use a water bucket against a barrier or another waterloggable block.
Let the map reject the placement.
Confirm only the acting player still sees water or waterlogged residue.
bugs.aiAnalysis: ArenaService treats buckets/water as dangerous and cancels the relevant interaction/item-use path for non-admin players. Runtime evidence shows the acting client can retain a predicted liquid/waterlogged representation after the server rejects the mutation. This is a client/server representation divergence, not a persistent shared-world water placement.

relevantCode.reason: DANGEROUS includes bucket/water and the before-event protection cancels restricted block interaction/item use.

bugs.suggestedFix: Prevent restricted liquid use before placement prediction where possible, or force authoritative block/state reconciliation after cancellation so the acting client clears ghost water.
mustPreserve: Normal allowed builder block placement inside the active plot.
Server-side protection against water and other restricted world mutations.

bugs.title: Roommaster/admin bypass can modify protected arena world
bugs.problem: A Roommaster with the map admin role bypasses build and dangerous-use guards, allowing protected arena blocks to be destroyed and restricted entities/items to be spawned or placed.
bugs.expected: Roommaster/admin access should preserve live arena geometry unless an explicit maintenance mode authorizes world mutation.
bugs.observed: Runtime testing shows Roommaster can destroy arena blocks and spawn entities; source bypasses build and interaction protection whenever isAdmin() is true.
reproduction: Join as the Roommaster/admin role used for map operation.
Move to protected arena geometry outside the active builder plot.
Break a protected block or use a restricted spawn/item interaction.
Confirm the arena world changes despite normal arena protection.
bugs.aiAnalysis: ArenaService.canBuild() immediately returns true for admins, protectInteraction() returns before all restrictions for admins, and the item-use danger guard only cancels non-admin sources. WorldData sets doMobSpawning=false, but that gamerule does not close admin/manual spawn paths. Arena destruction and manual entity spawning therefore share one causal root: blanket privileged world-mutation bypass.

relevantCode.reason: Admin users bypass canBuild(), interaction protection, and restricted item-use cancellation.
Defines the tag-based admin role consumed by the arena protection bypass.
doMobSpawning is already false, so manual/admin spawn paths must be distinguished from natural spawning.

bugs.suggestedFix: Replace the blanket admin world-mutation bypass with an explicit scoped maintenance mode; keep developer commands authorized while live arena geometry and restricted item use stay protected.
mustPreserve: Authorized debug/reset commands for map operators.
Normal builder construction inside the assigned active plot.
Normal entity setup owned by the map.

manualRuntimeEvidence.source: tester runtime feedback + selected-artifact source cross-check
manualRuntimeEvidence.notes: Physical arena escape was rejected after barrier containment was confirmed. Waterlogging client desync and Roommaster/admin world-mutation bypass were admitted. Entity spawning feedback is deduplicated into the Roommaster/admin bypass because doMobSpawning is already false and manual spawn paths share the permission root cause.
